# PA-2.4 eligibility proposal (A2)

Study: Gazley, B. (2008). Beyond the contract: The scope and nature of informal government–nonprofit partnerships. Public Administration Review, 68(1), 141–154.

Proposal: eligible.

## Reasons
1. Object is a relationship in a public service. The study examines service delivery partnerships between Georgia local governments (cities, counties) and charitable nonprofits in public service delivery or planning (p.141, p.144 survey question "collaborate with or involve nonprofit organizations in any form of public service delivery or planning"). Partnerships cover public safety, social, human and health services, economic development, parks, arts, environment (Table 5, p.150).
2. Quantitative findings. Two parallel mail surveys: 311 local government chief administrative officers (47% response, p.144) and 285 nonprofit executive directors (26.8% response, p.144). Frequencies and cross-tabulations in Tables 1-6 (p.144-150), chi-square tests (Table 6 note).
3. Qualitative findings. Five semistructured in-person interviews with Georgia public managers, July 2005 (p.144), reported with verbatim quotes (p.147).

## Points for A1
- The qualitative strand is small (five interviews, one page of results, p.147) and the author states that the interviews "are not generalizable" (p.147). The criterion (at least one qualitative finding) is met.
- Page numbers are the journal pagination (141-151); Tables 5 and 6 are on p.150.
